name: West Virginia
tagline: Coalfield hollows, spruce ridges, Civil War turnpikes and Eastern Panhandle river towns.
intro: West Virginia's byways follow old turnpikes over the Alleghenies, climb into the spruce of the Monongahela National Forest, wind through the company towns of the southern coalfields and loop through Washington's Eastern Panhandle. This chapter follows the West Virginia Byways and Backways program of the West Virginia Department of Transportation, Division of Highways, as drawn in its 2019 GIS layer and listed by Scenic America in 2023; the state publishes no current list of its own. A byway is a paved road, while a backway must be largely unpaved and give a rustic back-country trip, and several short backways are original pieces of the Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike.

members.name: Historic National Road
members.blurb: In West Virginia the old National Road is sixteen miles of US 40 across the Northern Panhandle, crossing the Ohio at Wheeling on a suspension bridge in use since 1849 and passing West Virginia Independence Hall.

members.name: Coal Heritage Trail
members.blurb: US 52 and WV 16 wind out of Bluefield through Welch and north toward Ansted, past tipples and company stores in the narrow hollows of the southern coalfields, and on through the historic districts of Bramwell and Mullens.

members.name: Highland Scenic Highway
members.blurb: From Richwood, WV 39 and the WV 150 parkway climb past Cranberry Glades into dark spruce above 4,500 feet, with four overlooks along the way and no winter plowing, before coming down to US 219 north of Marlinton.

members.name: Midland Trail
members.blurb: US 60 follows the old James River and Kanawha Turnpike from colonial Lewisburg down through the New River country at Hawks Nest to Malden, where Booker T. Washington grew up, and on into Charleston.

members.name: Washington Heritage Trail
members.blurb: A 136-mile loop through the Eastern Panhandle ties Harpers Ferry, Charles Town, Martinsburg and Berkeley Springs to the houses of Washington's kin, with a spur west to the Paw Paw Tunnel.

members.name: Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike
members.blurb: Claudius Crozet's toll road runs 180 miles from Parkersburg through Weston, Buckhannon and Beverly to just past Bartow, by the 1861 battle and camp sites on Rich Mountain, Cheat Mountain and Allegheny Mountain.

members.name: Back Mountain
members.blurb: A 2.7-mile stretch of the original Staunton-Parkersburg Turnpike climbs the east side of Cheat Mountain past houses that faced the main highway until US 250 took a straighter line in the 1950s.

members.name: Camp Allegheny
members.blurb: Ten gravel miles of the first turnpike descend Allegheny Mountain to Bartow, from the windswept earthworks of Camp Allegheny, held against a Union attack in December 1861, down to Traveller's Repose, a 19th-century inn.

members.name: Cheat Mountain
members.blurb: A short piece of the old turnpike switchbacks up from US 250 to Cheat Summit Fort, where Union troops held the mountaintop through the winter of 1861. Trails and an overlook now explain the earthworks.

members.name: Rich Mountain
members.blurb: From Beverly the old turnpike climbs Rich Mountain on about five miles of gravel to the battlefield of July 11, 1861, where soldiers' carvings still mark the rocks, then drops past the earthworks of Camp Garnett toward Mabie.

members.name: Cheat River
members.blurb: WV 72 follows the Cheat River Canyon for fourteen miles with Rowlesburg the only town on it, and its pull-offs look out on the Buckhorn Run waterfall and the B&O's Tray Run Viaduct.

members.name: Old Route 7
members.blurb: WV 7 leaves Morgantown up the rhododendron gorge of Deckers Creek, passes near the New Deal homestead town of Arthurdale, crosses the Cheat at Kingwood and climbs Briery Mountain to Terra Alta near the Maryland line.

members.name: Northwestern Turnpike
members.blurb: US 50 keeps to the 1830 Northwestern Turnpike over Laurel and Cheat mountains, the second with 28 curves on its grade, past the virgin forest of Cathedral State Park and the B&O railroad town of Grafton.

members.name: Little Kanawha Parkway
members.blurb: For 77 miles between I-79 and I-77 the road keeps company with the Little Kanawha River, through farm valleys and small towns like Glenville, past a steel truss bridge at Burnsville and a cable suspension bridge at Duck Run.

members.name: Farm Heritage Road
members.blurb: Monroe County's farm road follows the winding course of Indian Creek past its covered bridge, crosses the rolling farmland around the county seat of Union and ends in the Sweet Springs Valley under the long ridge of Peters Mountain.

members.name: Cedar Creek Road
members.blurb: Near the geographic center of the state, this backway follows Cedar Creek through hay meadows and pasture, mostly on one-lane blacktop with a few miles of gravel, by the old trading places of Cedarville and Exchange.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mountain's Shadow Trail
members.blurb: One-lane paved and gravel roads wander 29 miles past valley farms in the shadow of Peters Mountain, Monroe County's 40-mile ridge, with paths up to the Appalachian Trail and the Hanging Rock Observatory.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Wellsburg-Bethany
members.blurb: A short loop in Brooke County joins the Ohio River town of Wellsburg, laid out in 1790, with the college village of Bethany, where Alexander Campbell founded Bethany College in 1840.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Williams River
members.blurb: Narrow gravel forest roads follow the Williams River down from its mountain headwaters toward the Gauley near Cowen, a stocked trout stream with some thirty campsites by the water along the edge of the Cranberry Wilderness.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
